documents.title: Academic Integrity (policy)
documents.summary: Macalester's academic integrity page lists generative AI doing a student's work among examples of cheating. It has no other AI-specific provisions; sanctions and procedures are general.
documents.stance_why: The only AI language is that 'Having another person, or generative AI tools, do your work for a course' is cheating. It does not say AI is allowed with permission or give instructor options, so I coded restrict (AI doing the work is treated as a violation) rather than prohibit or delegates.

units.why: The cheating list names 'generative AI tools' doing 'your work for a course' as an example of cheating, so students must not have AI do their coursework. I chose P19 (no AI-produced submitted work) over P36 because the passage's content is the prohibited act; the misconduct label is its framing, and it is unqualified, so no instructor-permission language appears.
units.anchor: Having another person, or generative AI tools, do your work for a course
units.policy: Having generative AI tools do your work for a course is cheating.

documents.title: AI Guidelines for Faculty and Staff
documents.summary: ITS guidelines for faculty and staff using AI tools, covering data security, checking output, research and publication, and purchasing. It says nothing about student use.
documents.stance_why: The page offers 'suggestions for best practices' for employees who 'include AI tools in their work' and warns about data and output; it allows AI use with cautions, so permit, not delegates or encourage.

units.why: The scope paragraph states that the guidelines address faculty and staff use of software and data when including 'AI tools in their work', setting what the document covers.
units.anchor: written with the use of software and data by faculty for staff
units.frag_end: best practices when using AI and for AI tool procurement considerations & processes.

units.why: The page points faculty to the Library's LibGuide on 'AI Literacy and Critical Thinking' for classroom use; this is a resource for instructors learning about AI, so P63 rather than a stance type.
units.frag_start: If you’re looking for more info

units.why: Staff are told to 'Treat information given to an AI tool' as public and not share personal, confidential or proprietary data; this is data protection and tool-privacy advice, so P50.
units.anchor: do not share information that is personal, confidential, or proprietary intellectual property
units.frag_start: Treat information given to an AI tool

units.why: Staff are pointed to the Protecting Sensitive Information and Data Classification policies and told to avoid moderate or high-risk data in AI tools; a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: avoid entering data that may fall into the moderate or high-risk data categories

units.why: Users should be 'especially careful' with sensitive data given regulatory, contractual or legal obligations; this is advice using 'consider' and 'be careful', so should; data protection P50.
units.anchor: consider whether the data you are using will compromise regulatory, contractual, or legal obligations

units.why: Users are told to 'anonymize personally identifiable information' and use settings so inputs are 'not retained'; protecting personal data and tool retention is P50.

The page warns about 'intellectual property and confidentiality concerns' and says not to enter proprietary information. P50 (data protection) fits better than P52, which concerns copyright and ownership of AI output.
units.anchor: do not enter proprietary information into an AI tool

units.why: Users are told to 'Closely monitor output' because it may contain hallucinations, 'uncited intellectual property', errors and bias, and to use judgment; verification of AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Always use your judgment when analyzing AI responses

units.why: The Research and Publication section makes faculty 'individually responsible' for research integrity and tells them to follow funder and publication guidelines on generative AI, which is P62 (research and scholarship, deferring to venue/funder rules).
units.anchor: familiarize yourself with funding agency and publication guidelines to ensure compliance

units.why: Faculty and staff must 'contact ITS' when buying AI tools or adding them to software so security, reliability and performance are reviewed; institutional review of AI procurement (P65).
units.anchor: contact ITS so we can work through security, reliability, and performance concerns

units.why: The footer states 'Version: 1.1' and a 'Last Review' date, showing the guidance is versioned and reviewed; the text calls the landscape 'rapidly evolving'. This documents a review cycle (P54).

notes: Integrity page: only one sentence mentions AI; general sanction and procedure text (zero for first violation, consult student) was not coded as AI policy.
